verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same correct fix: an email-to-index Map built once, with new contacts registered as they are appended, so first-occurrence and in-upload merging behave as before. A adds a test for the one subtle behavior the Map has to keep, which is that duplicates already in the stored book send the merge to the first entry. A also measured the speedup and reports the test count accurately. B's code is equally correct and slightly more factored, but it leaves the first-occurrence behavior untested and does not measure the improvement.
a_issues: Benchmark was a throwaway script and not committed, so the 79 ms figure cannot be reproduced from the repo
b_issues: No test protects the first-occurrence choice when the existing book already contains duplicate emails, which is exactly what the Map-building logic must preserve
Speedup is unmeasured, so the report does not confirm the task's goal was met

verdict.rationale: Both changes swap the quadratic findIndex scan for the same Map-based lookup with the same first-occurrence semantics, so their correctness and scope are equivalent. B adds a test for the one subtle edge case the rewrite could break: duplicates already in the existing book must still merge into the first entry. B also measured the speedup and reported test and typecheck results concretely. A's small helper extraction is fine, but A leaves the edge case it describes untested and its speedup unmeasured.
a_issues: No test for merging into the first of several pre-existing duplicates, the edge case the map rewrite could most easily get wrong.
The speedup was not measured, so the performance claim is unverified.
b_issues: The timing came from a throwaway script, so no benchmark guards against future regressions.
